html:
Lalon, also called Lalon Fakir or Lalon Shah, was a Bengali mystic, songwriter and the most famous of the Baul singers, who lived at Cheuriya near Kushtia in western Bangladesh and died there in 1890.

Little is known of his early life, and Hindus and Muslims both claim him. His songs, passed down orally by his followers, ask what a person's caste or religion really is, and look for God within the human body. He wrote hundreds of them, simple in words and deep in meaning, sung with the one-stringed ektara.

Rabindranath Tagore, whose family owned land nearby, collected and admired them. Lalon's shrine at Kushtia holds a large festival each year. In Bangladesh, which has known clashes over religion, he stands for a tolerant folk faith that blends Sufism and Hindu devotion, as Chaitanya's followers did in Bengal before him.
sum: Lalon, also called Lalon Fakir or Lalon Shah, was a Bengali mystic, songwriter and the most famous of the Baul singers, who lived at Cheuriya near Kushtia in western Bangladesh and died there in 1890.
